chapter.name: Grassroots Democracy -- Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas

questions.q: 'Local Government is the base of India's governance pyramid, yet it is not one single body.' Justify this statement with five points from the chapter. (Fig. 12.2 shows the urban side running down from the urban local body, through the Ward Committee, to a bottom row labelled 'People of the Ward'.)
questions.a: 1. The chapter's pyramid places the Union Government at the national level at the top and the State Government below it. 2. Local Government forms the base, the level closer to the people. 3. Local Government splits into two sides: Panchayati Raj Institutions (rural) and urban local bodies (urban). 4. Even the urban side is not one body: its highest body may be a Municipal Corporation, a Municipal Council or a Nagar Panchayat, with ward committees below. 5. At the very bottom of the urban side are the people of the ward, so Local Government is a set of many bodies close to the people, not one office.
s: Union at the top, State below
Local Government at the base, closer to the people
Rural and urban branches
Several types of urban body with ward committees below
People of the ward at the bottom: many bodies, not one

questions.q: Explain, with three points, how Sidhwa's 1949 quote at the start of the chapter connects to the idea of participatory democracy in its introduction.
questions.a: 1. Participatory democracy means governance that empowers citizens to actively take part in the country's functioning. 2. Sidhwa wanted a full-fledged local body formed so that people would know what administration, the franchise, powers, rights and privileges are. 3. He wanted them to learn this in a small sphere, in their own town and village, which matches the chapter's point that participation happens at the local (rural and urban) levels as well as the state and national ones.
s: States what participatory democracy means
Sidhwa's aim: people knowing administration, franchise, powers, rights and privileges
Link: learnt in their own town and village, the local level of participation

questions.q: Priya's project on urban local bodies lists every function they carry out, from garbage collection to collecting taxes, and stops there. (a) Which of the chapter's two Big Questions has she left unanswered? (b) Give one point from the chapter that would begin to answer it.
questions.a: (a) The second Big Question: why urban local bodies are important in governance and democracy (her list answers only the first, what they are and what they do). (b) Any one of: they are decentralised, so local communities have a direct say on how their area is managed; they let citizens of an area come together and decide what is best for them, which is participatory democracy; they have elected members who represent local citizens.
s: (a) The second Big Question: why they are important in governance and democracy
(b) One supported point: direct say / citizens deciding together / elected members

questions.q:
Meghna prepared five sentences for a class talk on Chapter 12's introduction. Mark each sentence correct or incorrect, and rewrite each incorrect one so that it matches the chapter.
1. 'Participatory democracy is limited to the national and state levels.'
2. 'The chapter studies the urban side of the pyramid after Chapter 11 studied the rural side.'
3. 'Urban governance can be simpler than rural governance because cities are better organised.'
4. 'Rustom K. Sidhwa spoke as a member of the Constituent Assembly.'
5. 'The chapter promises to describe every detail of urban governance.'
questions.a: 1. Incorrect: participation can be at the rural, regional, urban, state or national level. 2. Correct. 3. Incorrect: the chapter says urban areas are generally more complex and diverse than rural ones, so urban governance needs to be more complex. 4. Correct (during the Constituent Assembly Debates, 13 October 1949). 5. Incorrect: the chapter says it will limit itself to the basic principles of urban governance.
s: Sentence 1 incorrect, corrected with the five levels
Sentence 2 correct
Sentence 3 incorrect, corrected: urban areas more complex and diverse, so governance more complex
Sentence 4 correct
Sentence 5 incorrect, corrected: only basic principles

questions.q: Which of these events comes closest to what Sidhwa hoped a local body would teach people, going by the words of his quote?
questions.a: A resident learns what powers her own town's body has and what her rights are
o: A resident learns what powers her own town's body has and what her rights are
A student learns how the Union Government at the top makes decisions for the country
A town hands its own decisions to a central authority at the top of the pyramid
A villager learns which State her village belongs to and who governs that State

questions.q: Kavya has finished Chapter 11 and is starting Chapter 12. Her teacher asks her to point to the side of the governance pyramid that each chapter explores. Which pairing is right?
questions.a: Chapter 11: the rural side; Chapter 12: the urban side
o: Chapter 11: the rural side; Chapter 12: the urban side
Chapter 11: the urban side; Chapter 12: the rural side
Chapter 11: the State level; Chapter 12: the Union level
Chapter 11: the national top; Chapter 12: the local base

questions.q:
Read the extract and answer.
'I desire that ... a full-fledged local body should be immediately formed, ... so that people may know really what is an administration, what are the franchise, what are the powers, what are the rights and what are the privileges in a small sphere, in their own town, in their own villages.'
A debate team must use this extract on the motion 'A town whose officials deliver every service well, with no residents taking part, already has the local body Sidhwa wanted.'
(a) In which forum was this said, and by what kind of member?
(b) The extract names no service such as roads or garbage. What, then, did the speaker expect a local body to give people? Explain using the words 'in a small sphere'.
(c) Which idea from the chapter's introduction, where citizens are empowered to take part, does this serve?
(d) Should the team speak for or against the motion? Decide, admitting what the motion gets right.
questions.a: (a) In the Constituent Assembly Debates (13 October 1949), by Rustom K. Sidhwa, a Member of the Constituent Assembly. (b) Knowledge and practice of self-government: people would come to know what administration, the franchise, powers, rights and privileges are, and 'in a small sphere' means they learn this close to home, in their own town or village, before the larger levels. (c) Participatory democracy: governance that empowers citizens to actively take part. (d) Against. The motion is right that delivering services is part of a local body's work (the chapter lists garbage collection, infrastructure and more), but Sidhwa wanted people themselves to learn administration and their rights, and the chapter says bodies work efficiently only when citizens also do their duties; a town with no residents taking part misses that.
s: (a) Constituent Assembly Debates, by a Member of the Constituent Assembly
(b) People learning administration, franchise, powers, rights close to home ('small sphere')
(c) Participatory democracy
(d) Against: services matter, but Sidhwa wanted citizens to take part and learn

questions.q: In a project, Riya writes: 'Rustom K. Sidhwa asked in 1949 for a full-fledged local body to be formed immediately, so India had no municipal body of any kind before 1949.' Which fact from the same chapter shows that her conclusion goes too far?
questions.a: The Madras Corporation was established in 1688
o: The Madras Corporation was established in 1688
Sidhwa was a member of the Constituent Assembly
Sidhwa spoke of local bodies in towns and villages
Local Government forms the base of the pyramid

questions.q: Kabir claims: 'India's governance pyramid has three levels, and urban local bodies are one of those three levels.' Test his claim against the chapter. Is he right, wrong or partly right? Explain.
questions.a: Partly right. The pyramid does have three levels: the Union Government at the national level, the State Government, and Local Government at the base. But urban local bodies are not a level of their own: they are one branch of Local Government, standing beside the Panchayati Raj Institutions on the rural side.
s: Verdict: partly right
Right part: three levels, Union, State and Local Government
Wrong part: urban local bodies are a branch of Local Government, beside Panchayati Raj Institutions

questions.q:
A Class 6 club is building a cardboard pyramid of India's system of governance for the school corridor. Before they glue anything, they must decide where each card goes. Their five cards read: 'Union Government', 'State Government', 'Local Government', 'Urban Local Bodies' and 'Panchayati Raj Institutions'. One member, Tanvi, argues: 'A pyramid's base is its widest row, so the Union Government, which serves the whole country, must go at the base.'
(a) Decide first: should the club accept Tanvi's plan? Give the chapter's own description of what the base of the pyramid stands for.
(b) Which card goes at the very top, and at what level does that body work?
(c) Two cards do not take a row of their own but branch out side by side. Name them and the card they branch from.
(d) A sixth card, 'Municipal Council', is found in the box. Under which of the five cards should it hang, and why not under the other branch?
questions.a: (a) No. The chapter says the base of the pyramid is the local level, closer to the people, so Local Government (not the Union Government) forms the base. (b) The Union Government goes at the top; it works at the national level. (c) Urban Local Bodies and Panchayati Raj Institutions branch side by side from Local Government (the urban and the rural side). (d) Under Urban Local Bodies: a Municipal Council is an urban local body on the urban side of the pyramid, while Panchayati Raj Institutions are the rural branch.
s: (a) Rejects the plan: the base is the local level, closer to the people
(b) Union Government at the top, national level
(c) Urban Local Bodies and Panchayati Raj Institutions branch from Local Government
(d) Municipal Council under Urban Local Bodies, the urban not the rural branch

questions.q: (a) A resident says the Union Government is 'the level closest to the people, because it governs every one of them'. Correct her, using the chapter's own description of the base of the governance pyramid. (b) Using your answer to (a), explain why a blocked drain in one lane is better known to a body at the base than to the Union Government at the top.
questions.a: (a) The chapter says the base of the pyramid is the local level (Local Government), the level closer to the people; the Union Government is at the top, at the national level. Governing everyone does not make it close to them. (b) Being closest to the people, the local level is where residents of that lane can directly raise the problem; the Union Government sits at the national level, farthest from the lane.
s: (a) Corrects her: the local level is the base, closer to the people; Union is the top, national level
(b) Uses (a): nearness to the people lets the local level know local problems

questions.q: A ward committee member in Pune and a Gram Panchayat member in a village near Pune work on different branches of the chapter's governance pyramid, yet both branches come out of the same level, called ___ Government. (Accept the level's one-word name, in any case.)
questions.a: Local

questions.q: Work backwards. A quiz card gives only this answer: 'Local Government'. Write a three-clue question for the card, using three different facts from the chapter, such that Local Government is the only possible answer.
questions.a: Model clues: (1) I am the level at the base of India's governance pyramid. (2) The chapter calls me the level closer to the people. (3) I branch into the Panchayati Raj Institutions on the rural side and urban local bodies on the urban side. Who am I? Any three correct clues that fit only Local Government are accepted.
s: A clue on its place at the base of the pyramid
A clue on being closer to the people
A clue on branching into rural and urban bodies, so only Local Government fits

questions.q: Place X is a village of about 900 people, most of them farming families. Place Y is a city of about 22 lakh people speaking many languages and doing many kinds of work. Using the chapter's reasoning, which conclusion follows?
questions.a: Y needs a more complex governance system, as it is more complex and diverse
o: Y needs a more complex governance system, as it is more complex and diverse
Y needs a simpler governance system, as a city has more officials to share the work
X and Y need the same governance system, as both belong to Local Government
X needs the more complex system, as its people make decisions as a community

questions.q: On the urban side of the chapter's governance pyramid (Fig. 12.2), the rows below Local Government run: urban local bodies, then ward committees, then a last row at the base. (a) Name the last row. (b) What does its place at the very bottom, the part the chapter calls closest to the people, tell you about where the urban system begins?
questions.a: (a) The people of the ward. (b) The urban system begins with ordinary residents of each ward, the people themselves, and builds up from them through the ward committee to the urban local body, rather than starting from an authority at the top.
s: (a) People of the ward
(b) The system starts from the residents of each ward, nearest the people, and builds upward

questions.q:
Read the statements about the chapter's picture of Indian governance.
1. In the pyramid, the State Government sits closer to the people than Local Government does.
2. Local Government branches into Panchayati Raj Institutions on one side and urban local bodies on the other.
3. The chapter calls good governance that lets citizens actively take part, from the rural to the national level, participatory democracy.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only
o: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q: Ishaan draws India's governance pyramid with the State Government at the base and Local Government in the middle. Which correction matches the chapter?
questions.a: Local Government belongs at the base, the level closer to the people
o: Local Government belongs at the base, the level closer to the people
The Union Government belongs at the base, as it serves the most people
The State Government belongs at the top, above the Union Government
Urban local bodies belong in the middle, above the State Government

questions.q: (a) In your own words, what does the chapter mean by participatory democracy? (b) Using (a), say whether the idea applies only to a country's national government, citing the levels the chapter lists.
questions.a: (a) Good governance that empowers citizens so they can actively take part in the country's functioning. (b) No. The chapter says this participation can be at the rural, regional, urban, state or national level, so it reaches down to local areas too.
s: (a) Governance that empowers citizens to actively take part
(b) Not only national: rural, regional, urban, state or national levels

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The chapter says the urban governance system needs to be more complex than the rural one.
Reason (R): Urban areas are generally more complex and diverse than rural areas.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: (a) Quote the words in Sidhwa's statement that show he wanted local bodies both in cities and in the countryside. (b) Match each of those words to the branch of Local Government in the chapter's pyramid that it corresponds to.
questions.a: (a) 'in their own town, in their own villages'. (b) 'Town' matches the urban branch, urban local bodies; 'villages' matches the rural branch, the Panchayati Raj Institutions.
s: (a) Quotes 'in their own town, in their own villages'
(b) Town: urban local bodies; villages: Panchayati Raj Institutions

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Ward committees keep an eye on anything that might go wrong in their area, such as a water leak or a blocked drain, and report it to the authorities.
Reason (R): The precise functioning of wards differs from State to State.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: 'A ward committee is the urban local body's eyes and hands in the neighbourhood.' Analyse this statement in five points, using the chapter's account of wards, ward committees and decentralisation. (In Fig. 12.2 the urban side runs, from the top down: the urban local body, then the Ward Committee, then the People of the Ward at the base.)
questions.a: 1. Cities and towns are divided into smaller units called wards, each with a ward committee. 2. In the pyramid, the ward committee sits between the urban local body above and the people of the ward below, so it is the link with residents. 3. Eyes: ward committees keep an eye on anything that might go wrong, such as a water leak, a blocked drain or a damaged road. 4. They report such problems to the authorities, so the larger body learns of them. 5. Hands: they facilitate activities such as health camps and campaigns against single-use plastics; and because the system is decentralised, local people have a direct say in this work.
s: Wards as small units, each with a committee
Place in the pyramid between the urban local body and the people
Watching for problems such as leaks, drains, roads
Reporting problems to the authorities
Facilitating activities, with local say under decentralisation

questions.q: A ward committee did four things this month. Which one is an example of keeping an eye on what might go wrong, rather than facilitating an activity?
questions.a: Telling the authorities about a leaking pipe
o: Telling the authorities about a leaking pipe
Holding a free health camp in the community hall
Running a drive against single-use plastic bags
Putting up posters for the camp

questions.q: After heavy rain, a stretch of road in Ward 14 of a city caves in. Which step matches what the chapter says ward committees do about such a problem?
questions.a: Report the damaged road to the authorities
o: Report the damaged road to the authorities
Ask the Union Government to come and repair it
Raise the ward's property tax to pay for it
Wait for the State to send new rules for wards

questions.q: Differentiate between a 'ward' and a 'ward committee', and say which of the two could organise a campaign against single-use plastics.
questions.a: A ward is an area: one of the smaller units into which a city or town is divided. A ward committee is the body for that ward, which facilitates activities and reports problems. The ward committee could organise the campaign; a ward, being an area, cannot.
s: Ward: a smaller unit (area) of a city or town
Ward committee: the body of the ward; it organises the campaign

questions.q: Interpret why the chapter describes urban local bodies as a way for 'local communities' to have 'a direct say'. Give three points, using wards and ward committees.
questions.a: 1. Urban local bodies are decentralised: they do not operate under one central authority at the top. 2. Cities and towns are split into wards, small units, so each area has its own ward committee. 3. Through the ward committee, the people of each ward come together, watch over and report their area's problems and run activities such as health camps, so they decide what is best for their own area.
s: Decentralised, not run by a central authority at the top
Cities divided into wards, each with a ward committee
Ward committees let the people of the area act and decide for their own area

questions.q:
Read the statements about wards.
1. Cities and towns are divided into smaller units called wards.
2. A ward committee is the body that decides matters for the whole State.
3. In the chapter's pyramid, the ward committee sits above the urban local body it belongs to.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: 1 only
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only

questions.q: In Town P, every decision about its street lights is taken by one office at the top that serves the whole State. In Town Q, the people of each area have a direct say on how their lights are managed. Which town's system is decentralised in the chapter's sense?
questions.a: Town Q, as the local community has a direct say
o: Town Q, as the local community has a direct say
Town P, as one central authority keeps it uniform
Town P, as the State level is closest to people
Neither, as only villages can be decentralised

questions.q: Write a short decision note (five points) for a city that must choose between Plan 1, 'one committee for the whole city, meeting at the city centre', which costs less and keeps one routine for all areas, and Plan 2, 'a committee in every ward'. The city's two aims are that problems are found quickly and that residents have a direct say. Choose the plan that meets both aims, justify it from the chapter, and name one thing a ward committee still depends on others for.
questions.a: 1. Choice: Plan 2, a committee in every ward, because the city's two aims outweigh the savings of Plan 1. 2. Cities and towns are divided into wards, and ward committees keep an eye on what might go wrong nearby, such as a water leak, a blocked drain or a damaged road, so problems are found quickly. 3. Urban local bodies are decentralised: local communities have a direct say on how their own area is managed, which meets the second aim. 4. Plan 1 works like a central authority at the top, the opposite of what the chapter describes, even if it is cheaper. 5. A ward committee still depends on the authorities: the chapter says it reports problems to them, so it relies on them to act.
s: Chooses Plan 2 because of the two aims
Ward committees find problems near home
Decentralisation gives residents a direct say
Plan 1 is a central authority at the top despite costing less
Depends on the authorities it reports to

questions.q: A local newspaper headline reads: 'Ward 9 residents meet, choose where the new dustbins go'. Give two features of urban local bodies described in the chapter that this headline illustrates.
questions.a: 1. Cities and towns are divided into smaller units called wards (Ward 9). 2. Urban local bodies are a mechanism for citizens living in an area to come together and take decisions about what is best for them (the residents choosing the dustbin spots).
s: City divided into wards
Citizens of an area come together to decide what is best for them

questions.q:
A city ran its ward health camps two ways in two years. Year 1: each ward committee picked the date and place after asking the ward's residents. Year 2: one office at the city centre fixed every camp and simply informed the wards.
(a) Which year's method fits the chapter's description of urban local bodies as decentralised? Explain using what the chapter says decentralised means.
(b) Using (a), say what the residents lost in Year 2.
questions.a: (a) Year 1. The chapter says decentralised means that instead of operating under a central authority at the top, local communities have a direct say on how their areas are managed; in Year 1 each ward decided its own camp. (b) In Year 2 the residents lost their direct say: a central office decided for them, so they could no longer come together and decide what is best for their own ward.
s: (a) Year 1, with the meaning: local direct say instead of a central authority at the top
(b) Uses (a): residents lost their direct say over their own ward

questions.q: Meera moves from a city in one State to a city in a neighbouring State and finds that her new ward does things a little differently. Which explanation fits the chapter?
questions.a: Each State makes its own rules for wards
o: Each State makes its own rules for wards
Her new city must not have urban local bodies at all
Only her old city was divided into separate wards
The Union Government gives each city a new ward plan

questions.q:
A water pipe bursts in a lane of Kanpur city, and another bursts in a village 20 km away.
(a) Name the branch of Local Government in the chapter's pyramid that serves each place.
(b) In the city, which small unit is the lane part of, and which body there would, going by the chapter, notice the burst pipe and pass it on? To whom?
questions.a: (a) Kanpur city: the urban branch, its urban local bodies; the village: the rural branch, the Panchayati Raj Institutions. (b) The lane is part of a ward; the ward committee keeps an eye on problems such as a water leak and reports them to the authorities.
s: (a) City: urban local bodies; village: Panchayati Raj Institutions
(b) A ward; its ward committee reports the leak to the authorities

questions.q: A resident claims: 'A ward committee's only job is to complain to the authorities when something breaks.' Test the claim against the chapter. Is it right, wrong or partly right? Give reasons.
questions.a: Partly right. Ward committees do keep an eye on anything that might go wrong, such as a water leak, a blocked drain or a damaged road, and report such problems to the authorities. But that is not their only job: they also facilitate activities such as conducting health camps and organising campaigns against single-use plastics.
s: Verdict: partly right
Right part: they watch for and report problems to the authorities
Wrong part: they also facilitate activities such as health camps and plastics campaigns

questions.q: True or False? 'A free health camp for the residents of a city ward would be arranged through the Gram Panchayat, as health camps are a village matter.' Give the verdict and the corrected statement.
questions.a: False. The Gram Panchayat belongs to the rural side of the pyramid (Panchayati Raj Institutions). In a city, it is the ward committee that facilitates activities such as conducting health camps for its ward.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: in a city the ward committee facilitates health camps; the Gram Panchayat is rural

questions.q: Sneha says: 'An urban local body is just a branch office that carries out orders sent down from the top.' Which reply fits the chapter best?
questions.a: No: it lets citizens of an area come together and decide what is best for them
o: No: it lets citizens of an area come together and decide what is best for them
Yes: it sits below the State Government in the pyramid, so it only obeys orders
No: it takes its orders from the Union Government, never from the State level
Yes: only Panchayati Raj bodies let people decide things for their own area

questions.q:
Two friends compare their cities.
Farhan (City A, State X): 'Our ward committee meets every month and must send a report to the city body after each meeting.'
Lata (City B, State Y): 'Our ward committee meets when residents ask, and it reports problems as they come up.'
Farhan says, 'One of our cities must be breaking the rules, because ward committees should all work the same way.'
(a) Is Farhan right? Decide first, and give the chapter's reason.
(b) What do both committees have in common, going by what the chapter says all ward committees do?
(c) Farhan's committee reports to 'the city body'. Where does that body sit in the chapter's pyramid compared with the ward committee, and what kinds of body can it be?
(d) Lata says her system is 'more decentralised' because residents call the meetings. Using the chapter's meaning of 'decentralised', judge whether her reasoning holds, and say what the chapter does not tell us.
questions.a: (a) No. The chapter says the precise functioning of wards differs from State to State, depending on the rules each State makes, so different patterns in States X and Y need not break any rule. (b) Both report problems to the authorities; both are committees of a ward, a smaller unit of the city. (c) Directly above the ward committee: it is the city's urban local body, a Municipal Corporation, a Municipal Council or a Nagar Panchayat. (d) Partly sound: decentralised means local communities have a direct say on their own area, and residents calling meetings fits that; but the chapter does not compare or rank one State's ward rules against another's, so it gives no ground to call either system more decentralised.
s: (a) Not right: ward functioning differs from State to State
(b) Both report problems to the authorities; both are ward units
(c) The urban local body above: Corporation, Council or Nagar Panchayat
(d) Partly sound under direct say, but the chapter does not rank State rules

questions.q:
Match each event in a city ward with the chapter's idea it shows.
Column A:
1. Residents of Ward 5 decide together where their new benches go.
2. A committee member tells the authorities about a damaged road.
3. The ward committee runs a camp where doctors check residents.
4. Wards in two States follow different procedures.
Column B:
a. Ward committees facilitate activities
b. Decentralisation: local communities have a direct say
c. Rules made by each State
d. Ward committees watch for and report problems

Ward 22 of a city kept this log for one week.
Monday: a drain outside the school is blocked.
Tuesday: the ward committee holds a free health camp; 140 residents come.
Wednesday: a water pipe on Lake Road is leaking.
Thursday: the committee starts a campaign against single-use plastic bags at the vegetable market.
Friday: a pothole opens on the main road.
(a) Sort the five entries into two groups: problems the committee should watch for, and activities the committee facilitates.
(b) To whom should the committee pass the entries in the first group?
(c) A resident asks why the committee runs the camp itself but only passes on the leak. Using the chapter's two verbs for ward committees, 'facilitate' and 'report', explain the difference in its role.
(d) The drain was reported on Monday and work starts tomorrow. The leak and the pothole have not been reported, and the committee can send only one urgent report today. One member says 'the pothole, because someone could be hurt'; another says 'the leak'. Decide, and say which choice the chapter itself gives a reason for and what the chapter leaves unsettled.
questions.a: (a) Problems to watch: Monday drain, Wednesday pipe leak, Friday pothole. Activities facilitated: Tuesday health camp, Thursday plastics campaign. (b) To the authorities. (c) For activities such as health camps and campaigns the committee facilitates: it makes them happen in its ward. For problems such as leaks it keeps an eye on them and reports them to the authorities, who act on them. (d) Either choice is accepted with a reason. The chapter's own reason supports the leak: reporting a water leakage promptly prevents further wastage of precious water. The chapter gives no reason about potholes and does not rank one problem above another, so the safety argument comes from outside the chapter; both should be reported as soon as possible.
s: (a) Drain, leak, pothole as problems; camp and campaign as activities
(b) Report to the authorities
(c) Facilitates activities itself; reports problems for the authorities to act on
(d) A reasoned choice, noting the chapter's reason (prompt reporting saves water) covers the leak and the chapter does not rank the two

questions.q: A student's chart names 'Ward Committee' as the highest urban local body of a large city. Show, from the chapter, that a ward committee cannot be a city's highest urban body. Give three points. (In Fig. 12.2 the urban side runs, from the top down: Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Nagar Panchayat; then Ward Committee; then People of the Ward.)
questions.a: 1. A ward is only one of the smaller units into which a city is divided, so a ward committee speaks for one part of the city, not the whole. 2. In the chapter's pyramid, the ward committee sits below the urban local body (a Municipal Corporation, a Municipal Council or a Nagar Panchayat) and above only the people of the ward. 3. When the chapter names the highest body of a city, it names one of those three types, never a ward committee: Chennai and Indore have a Municipal Corporation at the top of their urban bodies, and the type depends on the city's population.
s: A ward is one smaller unit of the city
Pyramid: ward committee below the urban local body, above the people
The chapter's highest bodies are Corporation, Council or Nagar Panchayat (e.g. Chennai, Indore), never a ward committee

questions.q: A scheme of the government promises new water connections to poor families. City officials go house to house to see whether the families really got them. Which function of urban local bodies is this?
questions.a: Checking the implementation of government schemes
o: Checking the implementation of government schemes
Planning for the area's economic and social development

Corporation's cleanliness services: solid waste management, debris clearance
Matches the function of garbage collection and disposal
Efficiency needs citizens' duties, e.g. waste segregation
Judgement: 'alone' goes too far; joint work in a participatory democracy

questions.a: Yes, he is right. Payments: property tax (and water charges) are money citizens pay the corporation. Papers: the marriage certificate (and licences such as business, hoardings and trade licenses) are papers the corporation issues. Complaints: CRM - grievances is where citizens' complaints are dealt with. He says 'at least', so the figure's other services, such as fire services, do not make him wrong.

Complaints: CRM - grievances

questions.q: A town of 6,40,000 people has a Nagar Palika as its highest urban body. For it to have a Mahanagar Nigam instead, its population must grow by more than ___ lakh.

The population of a growing town, Navgaon, was counted every ten years.
2006: 92,000
2016: 1,85,000
2026: 3,60,000
In 2026 some members of the town's highest body want to start calling it the 'Navgaon Mahanagar Nigam', saying the name will attract investors.
(a) What was the town's highest urban body in 2006?
(b) What was it in 2016? Give both of the names the chapter uses for it.
(c) Should the body take the name 'Mahanagar Nigam' in 2026? Decide, using the chapter's rule.
(d) If the town keeps growing by the same number of people every ten years as it did from 2016 to 2026, in which count year will it first be large enough for a Mahanagar Nigam?
questions.a: (a) A Nagar Panchayat, as 92,000 is below 1 lakh. (b) A Municipal Council, also called the Nagar Palika, as 1,85,000 is between 1 and 10 lakh. (c) No: a Mahanagar Nigam (Municipal Corporation) is only for cities above 10 lakh, and 3,60,000 is below that, so the town still has a Municipal Council. (d) The growth is 3,60,000 - 1,85,000 = 1,75,000 per ten years: 2036: 5,35,000; 2046: 7,10,000; 2056: 8,85,000; 2066: 10,60,000. So in 2066 it first passes 10 lakh.
s: (a) Nagar Panchayat
(b) Municipal Council (Nagar Palika)
(c) No: still below 10 lakh
(d) 2066, with growth of 1,75,000 per decade

questions.q:
Mrs Sharma lives in Indore. (a) Under which headings of the figure do the tax and the hoarding fall?

(d) Not sound: the list is simplified

s: (a) Property tax and water charges
(b) Collecting local taxes and fines; money funds the services

questions.q: A dead tree leans over Mrs Joshi's house in Indore; she wants it cut down and the wood carried away. Her friend says, 'Every service in Indore's list is a CRM service, so look under a CRM heading.' Where should she look?

CRM - grievances, since every one of the services is CRM

Similarity: people act together or report problems in both
